_comment: tiles 3.0 (/tiles) — rebuilt from scratch alongside tiles2. Three things make it different: (1) outline_mode=segmentation, so no baked outline to post-process away; (2) the FLAT BASE TILE — every ground type must have one tile whose top surface is a single flat colour, so the game can fill huge areas with it and the player can never see where the repeat starts; (3) every ground type is generated OVER every other, so the map agent picks the walkable TOP and the sideways WALL independently. Transitions/cliffs/slopes come from /create-tileset (lower+upper+spread_x/slope_size/raggedness), not from per-pair sheets. No tiles taller than 1 level — scenery owns objects now.
_prompt_comment: THE KEY LESSON from the maintainer's own prompt tests: naming the MATERIAL gets you texture you cannot flatten ('clean single colour grass' still returns detailed grass). Naming the COLOUR gets you the flat fill we actually want. So every type carries `color_words` used to build prompts, and `material_words` kept only for the later detailed-variant pass. `hex` is the intended resting colour — the QA target the generated top is measured against, not something sent to the API.
_base_prompt_comment: MEASURED, not guessed. An 8-strategy bake-off (identical pinned harness, only the prompt varying; see docs/BAKEOFF.md) settled these. Three results shaped the templates below: (1) flatness is EASY — five different prompts reached share >= 0.99, so it is not the discriminator; (2) COLOUR ACCURACY is the hard part, and only anchoring an explicit #hex landed it (dE 5.7 vs 21-31 for every prompt that named the colour in words alone) — which is why every template carries {hex}; (3) naming the material ('single color 100% pure green') is read as a STYLE hint and ignored as an instruction: it scored 0.825 with visible grass blades. Long negation lists ('no texture, no pattern, no speckles...') do work but drift the hue badly on their own. Ask for a flat surface AND pin the hex.

prompts.flat_base: solid uniform #{hex} {color}, one single flat colour, completely smooth, no texture
prompts.over: isometric tile with a completely flat uniform #{top_hex} {top_color} top surface and plain #{side_hex} {side_color} side walls, no texture on the top, no outline

_accept_comment: A candidate base tile must clear ALL of these. share/dE alone are gameable: two bake-off prompts scored a PERFECT 1.000 by returning a plain shaded cube with no distinct wall and (in one case) undersized art that would not tessellate — flawless by the metric, useless as a tile. Hence geom_ok.
